s: A SaaS company wants to prove before every major release that its application, which runs across three Availability Zones, survives the loss of one AZ. That includes EC2 instances, the Aurora writer, and ElastiCache nodes in the AZ. The test must stop automatically if the customer-facing error rate goes above 2%. The company wants to write as little custom code as possible. Which solution meets these requirements?
o: Run an AWS Resilience Hub assessment against the application before each release, and block the release if the estimated RTO exceeds policy.

Write AWS Lambda functions that terminate instances in one AZ, reboot the Aurora writer with failover, and fail over the ElastiCache primary. Have an engineer watch dashboards and stop the test manually.
Use AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks to stop the EC2 instances in one AZ, and use a CloudWatch alarm to send an Amazon SNS notification to the team when the error rate rises.

Create an AWS Fault Injection Service experiment template from the AZ Availability: Power Interruption scenario, and configure a stop condition that uses a CloudWatch alarm on the 2% error-rate metric.

w.y: The FIS scenario library includes a prebuilt AZ power-interruption scenario that affects compute, Aurora, ElastiCache, and more. FIS stop conditions tied to CloudWatch alarms halt the experiment automatically. That meets 'stop automatically' and 'as little custom code as possible'.

o.A: Resilience Hub estimates resilience from configuration. It does not inject a real failure to prove survival.
o.B: This is heavy custom code, and a manual stop does not satisfy the automatic stop requirement.
o.C: This covers only EC2, and an SNS notification does not stop the experiment.
o.D: Correct: a prebuilt FIS AZ scenario with an alarm-based stop condition.

d: stop automatically at 2% errors; least custom code
